$comment: Witnesses whose evidence changed when the quotient gained a declared codomain (ANALYTICAL-QUOTIENT-CODOMAIN-AUTHORITY-01). Each is HELD OPEN, not decided: no standing moves because this file exists. The ledger may only shrink — `necessity.test.ts` refuses an entry whose witness holds again, and refuses a non-holding witness that is not listed, so neither a stale entry nor a new failure can hide here. What remains is one defect seen twice: A HOLE IS OBSERVABLE WHERE AN ABSENCE WAS NOT. Deleting a required discriminator destroyed the evidence that betrays its branch; holing it leaves that evidence standing. The old erasures did not hold these coordinates apart — they hid the residue by destroying it, and nobody had stated that as the argument. Reverting to deletion is refused on its own terms: it produces images the representation cannot express (`quotientLanguageInvalid`), which is what this spec exists to end.

awaiting.detail: The pair is FX_TEMP_RATIO_COMPARISON against FX_N_TEMP_MEAN. `assertion.aggregate.op` is branch-qualified — the slot exists only where kind is `aggregate` — so after both erasures the aggregate side carries `op: <hole>` and the ratio-comparison side carries no `op` slot at all. The PRESENCE of the hole betrays the branch that the `kind` erasure was supposed to forget. Deletion hid this by removing the slot; it did not forget it.
awaiting.repair: This is exactly the residue the closure form exists to normalize: a `forget-branch-field` carrier over the aggregate branch's `op`, carrier `assertion.kind:aggregate~ratio-comparison`. No such carrier is ledgered in closures-stage2.json -- its 22 carriers are relation.derivedBy.kind and field.additivity.kind pairs. It is mechanically derivable rather than argued: residue aggregate:[op], unilateral, minRawEdit 2, footprint of 7 coordinates. MEASURED, not assumed. Run through checkClosure on the closure's own stimulus pair -- FX_TEMP_RATIO_COMPARISON against that fixture with the assertion rewritten to an aggregate mean -- obligations 1 through 6 ALL HOLD, obligation 3 among them, reporting `identical outside assertion`. An earlier revision of this entry recorded a checker limit here (that the instrument could not evaluate obligation 3 for an assertion holder because no locator was keyed by that path); that limit no longer exists -- 79279322 locates a discriminated holder from its leaf, and a positional holder is HOLED rather than deleted so the image stays expressible. What remains is two facts and neither is a tooling limit. Obligation 7 is INDETERMINATE BY CONSTRUCTION: no sibling pair on assertion.kind has a compatible branch payload signature, so no same-enum control can exist, and assertion.kind has exactly two members -- its only member pair IS this carrier. The closure form cannot be discharged for this carrier whatever the dependencies do, which is a property of the instrument rather than of the residue. Obligation 8 then fails as well: all 7 footprint coordinates hold primitive standing, so the carrier cannot be proven primitive through this closure and composite constructor versus derived discriminator must be re-decided. Promoting it would therefore gain nothing, and it is not ledgered; the question this leaves is what the proof form is for a two-member discriminated union, which by construction cannot supply the control that form requires.

awaiting.detail: The same pair and the same residue as above, reached through the member-class spelling instead of the whole-leaf one: both sides carry `kind` as the class {aggregate, ratio-comparison}, and the aggregate side still carries `op: <hole>` that the other side has no slot for. That the two spellings fail identically is the point — the residue is a property of the branch structure, not of which erasure names it.
awaiting.repair: The same carrier settles both entries, and the measurement recorded above applies to both spellings: obligations 1 through 6 hold, obligation 7 is indeterminate because assertion.kind supplies no payload-compatible sibling, and obligation 8 fails on a primitive footprint. If the form could ever be discharged, this entry and the one above would close together; while it cannot be, both coordinates keep their present evidence and neither entry should be read as awaiting a repair that the closure form can perform.
